subject: BlueHarbor — Recap & next steps (cost discovery)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Park <alan.park@blueharbor.ai>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-09T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: BlueHarbor — Recap & next steps (cost discovery)

Hi Alan / Emily — thanks again for the 45m today. Below is a short recap to make sure we captured priorities and next steps correctly. If anything below is off, reply with edits.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary pain: rising inference cost for real-time scoring of document embeddings and chat assistant (esp. long-context customer docs).
- Unit economics target: need ~3x reduction in $/1000 tok on current monthly batch profile to justify migration (current spend ~ $45k / month for inference).
- Latency constraint: p95 < 350ms for short queries (<=1024 tokens); longer batch jobs can be >1s.
- Ops requirement: private VPC deployment or strict egress controls — data residency discussion ongoing.

Current stack
- Models: mix of open Llama variants and a smaller Flan-T5 family for reranking; currently hosted on managed endpoints (SageMaker) with autoscaling.
- Cache/batching today: none for interactive assistant; nightly batch for embeddings.

Success criteria for a pilot (what would make this a win?)
- Proof point: end-to-end inference cost reduction of ~30–50% for production-like traffic.
- Latency: meet p95 <= 350ms on interactive queries.
- Functional parity: comparable answer quality for our prompts (we agreed on a 20-prompt eval set).

Technical openness and constraints
- Quantization: team is open to int8/4-bit if accuracy drop is minimal.
- Acceptable rollbacks: must have fallback to current model variant during rollout windows.

Next steps (owner / ETA)
1) Rishi / Redwood: share a first-pass TCO workbook + sample config options (attached) — by EOD 5/9.
2) BlueHarbor: share a) 7-day representative API traces and b) top-20 prompts for quality eval — by 5/12.
3) Marissa (SE): propose a pilot architecture (Dedicated vs Private options) and run a short quantization sensitivity test once artifacts arrive — by 5/14.
4) Schedule pilot kickoff + 1h walkthrough with engineering (aim week of 5/18) — Rishi to propose times.

Attachments: redwood_tco_estimate_v1.xlsx (cost scenarios), redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf (pilot SOW template).

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alan Park <alan.park@blueharbor.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-09T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor — Recap & next steps (cost discovery)

Thanks Rishi — great capture. A few clarifications inline: 

> Primary pain: rising inference cost for real-time scoring of document embeddings and chat assistant (esp. long-context customer docs).
This is correct — our quarterly spend is spiking because of increased query volume and longer contexts as we index larger customer datasets.

> Unit economics target: need ~3x reduction in $/1000 tok on current monthly batch profile to justify migration (current spend ~ $45k / month for inference).
To be explicit: we need to see a path to 2.5x–3x improvement on average, willing to accept smaller gains on the first pass as long as the roadmap to target is clear.

> Current stack — Models: mix of open Llama variants and a smaller Flan-T5 family for reranking; currently hosted on managed endpoints (SageMaker) with autoscaling.
Correct. Also running a small GPU cluster for internal experiments (k8s + private registry) but not production.

Action: we will pull the 7-day API traces and the 20 prompts. Expect that to hit you by 5/11 (we have to scrub PII).

One operational ask: we will need a non-prod Private deployment option for the pilot (VPC peering) — Marissa, happy to sync on connectivity.

—Alan
Alan Park
Head of ML — BlueHarbor Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Park <alan.park@blueharbor.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-09T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor — Recap & next steps (cost discovery)

Alan — thanks. Quick technical notes from my side after listening in: 
- Batching/caching: we can introduce request-level prefix caching for the assistant layer and dynamic batching for near-real-time scoring. That typically yields 20–40% token savings depending on prompt overlap.
- Quantization path: we can start with a post-training int8 pass; if you want to push further we have a 4-bit recipe (requires validation against your 20-prompt set).
- Latency expectations: with Dedicated capacity and smart routing we should be able to hit p95 <= 350ms on <=1024-token queries for most model variants — will confirm once we have traces.

I attached a short technical checklist and the SOW draft (redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf). The checklist lists the artifacts we need: sample traces, eval prompts, and an initial test dataset (nlp-safe subset).

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-se-checklist.md (stub), redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@blueharbor.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alan Park <alan.park@blueharbor.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor — Recap & next steps (cost discovery)

Appreciate the clear summary. From a product leadership perspective:
- We are open to a two-phase pilot: Phase 1 (cost/latency validation on a subset of traffic), Phase 2 (expanded rollout + security/compliance review).
- Compliance: expect a short questionnaire on data retention and audit logs — can Redwood provide an example SOC-2 evidence pack or a list of relevant audit artifacts for Private deployments?

We will prioritize sending traces + prompts this week. Looking forward to Marissa's connectivity notes.

Emily Chen
VP Engineering | BlueHarbor Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Park <alan.park@blueharbor.ai>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@blueharbor.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor — Recap & next steps (cost discovery)

Great — thanks all. Quick summary of agreed immediate items and owners: 
- Rishi: updated TCO + simple runbook for pilot (attached workbook v1) — DONE (see attachment).
- BlueHarbor: traces + eval prompts by 5/11 (Alan).
- Marissa: send connectivity checklist + ideal test VM spec for Private pilot by 5/12.
- Scheduling: proposing 3 options for kickoff week of 5/18 — I will send a Doodle in the next hour.

If there are no objections Ill pull these into the HubSpot deal and draft a short SOW for legal review.

Best — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
